project_specification.project_name: nullius — Stage 1 BingX VST mirror: place the dry-run plan on the demo venue
project_specification.addition_summary:
Extend the router workspace member (packages/router, import name router) so the Stage 0 dry-run plan can be placed on BingX's VST (demo) perpetual swap venue. Stage 0 already turns a book into would-send orders without touching the network: router.bingx_documents reads the contracts and mark prices, router.sizing sizes weights into contract deltas, router.bingx_client_order_id projects the 40-character clientOrderID, and router.bingx_dry_run.dry_run_plan assembles the plan through the router's gates. Stage 1 adds four pieces. A signed BingX client, written over the standard library, can only reach open-api-vst.bingx.com: the live host is refused in code, with no flag. A preflight checks the venue before anything is placed. An order read-back reports status and cancels. A mirror command places the plan through the router's existing idempotent placement store, weight limiter and backoff, so a re-run never places an order twice.
BingX facts this spec relies on, checked against BingX's published API documentation (bingx-api.github.io/docs) and its sample code. A signed request adds timestamp (milliseconds) and recvWindow to its parameters, sorts them by key, URL-encodes them, computes HMAC-SHA256 of that query string keyed by the secret, appends signature=hex, and sends the key in the X-BX-APIKEY header. Responses are {"code": 0, "msg": "", "data": ...}, where a non-zero code is a refusal. HTTP 429 means the rate limit was hit. clientOrderID is "a limit of characters from 1 to 40. Different orders cannot use the same clientOrderID". timeInForce supports PostOnly. Margin modes are ISOLATED and CROSSED. Endpoints (all under https://open-api-vst.bingx.com) are: - GET /openApi/swap/v2/server/time (public) - GET /openApi/swap/v2/quote/contracts (public) - GET /openApi/swap/v2/quote/premiumIndex (public) - GET /openApi/swap/v2/user/balance - GET /openApi/swap/v2/user/positions - POST /openApi/swap/v2/trade/marginType - POST /openApi/swap/v2/trade/leverage - POST /openApi/swap/v2/trade/order - GET /openApi/swap/v2/trade/order - DELETE /openApi/swap/v2/trade/order - GET /openApi/swap/v2/trade/openOrders

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (members under packages/*, composed by src/app/module_loader.create_app) / SQLite stores addressed by DATABASE_URL / pytest (ruff conventions)
existing_context.test_baseline: workspace suite tests/ and member suites under packages/*/tests passing on main; packages/router/tests has 872 passing. Measure the real numbers by running the suites before relying on them.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, stdlib-first members (the router adds no third-party dependency), docstrings citing app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, refusals raised as typed errors whose message opens with a greppable code word and names the one repair, defined in the module that raises them and subclassing router.errors.RouterError (router.errors and router/__init__.py are not edited). Money and quantities are decimal.Decimal built from the venue's strings. Cross-member imports (book, risk) are deferred past module scope. Tests assert observed behaviour with narrative docstrings and never reach the network: the client takes an injected transport, and the end-to-end test serves a BingX stand-in on 127.0.0.1. Member suites run with PYTHONPATH=src:packages/router/src:packages/book/src:packages/ingest/src:packages/risk/src. Existing pieces Stage 1 must reuse rather than reimplement: - router.bingx_dry_run.dry_run_plan(book=, contracts=, marks=); - router.bingx_documents.resolve_bingx_filters and resolve_bingx_mark_prices; - router.submission_result.RouterOrderPlacementStore.place(order, place, now=), which places once per client_order_id and returns the prior result on a repeat; - router.limiter.RouterRateLimiter.acquire(operation) with a VenueWeightSchedule; - router.retry.retry_rate_limited(request, retries=), which retries on RouterRateLimitedError; - risk.kill.require_orders_allowed, which refuses while a kill instruction stands.

category.name: BingX VST Mirror
category.feature: System delivers BingX swap requests only to open-api-vst.bingx.com, each signed: a request carries timestamp and recvWindow, its parameters sorted by key and URL-encoded, signature equal to the HMAC-SHA256 hex of that query string keyed by the secret, and the key in the X-BX-APIKEY header. A request addressed to any other host, open-api.bingx.com included, returns a live_host_refused refusal before anything is sent. A response whose code is not 0 returns a bingx_refused error carrying that code and msg. HTTP 429 raises router.errors.RouterRateLimitedError. Credentials are read from BINGX_VST_API_KEY and BINGX_VST_SECRET_KEY; a missing one returns a vst_credentials_missing refusal naming the variable, and neither value appears in any repr, message or log line. The client exposes server time, balance, positions, set margin type, set leverage, place order, query order, cancel order and open orders.

System runs a VST preflight before any placement and returns a PreflightReport, or the first refusal, in this order: - orders_killed while risk.kill.require_orders_allowed refuses; - clock_skew when the venue's server time differs from the local clock by more than 1000 ms; - hedge_mode when any position reports positionSide LONG or SHORT, with the repair "switch the VST account to one-way mode"; - insufficient_balance when available USDT is below the book's equity_usdt. For each symbol the plan will order, it then sets margin type ISOLATED and leverage 1, treating an already-set answer as success. The report records the measured skew, the available balance and the symbols prepared.

System returns each of the book's VST orders, looked up by clientOrderID, with its status (NEW, PARTIALLY_FILLED, FILLED, CANCELED, EXPIRED or not_found), its executed quantity and its average price. Asked to cancel, it returns the identifiers of the open orders it cancelled: only those whose clientOrderID belongs to the book's rebalance. Orders from any other book or rebalance are left untouched.

System mirrors a book onto VST from `python -m router.bingx_mirror --book BOOK`. It fetches the contracts and premiumIndex documents from VST, replaces the book's positions with the account's live VST positions, and builds the plan with dry_run_plan. - Without --place it prints the plan in Stage 0's JSON-lines format and exits 0 while placing nothing. - With --place it requires DATABASE_URL and runs the preflight. Then it places each order through RouterOrderPlacementStore.place, acquiring RouterRateLimiter weight and retrying 429s with retry_rate_limited. It prints one JSON line per leg: placed, prior (already placed), or refused with its code. It exits 0 when every order was placed or was already placed, and 1 otherwise. - When a POST /trade/order times out or its connection drops, the outcome is unknown. The mirror then queries that clientOrderID before doing anything else. A found order is recorded as placed, and only a not_found answer is re-posted, so a blind retry never meets BingX's duplicate-clientOrderID refusal for an order that actually landed. - --status prints feature 3's read-back, and --cancel cancels the rebalance's open orders. The end-to-end test runs the command against a BingX stand-in on 127.0.0.1 that verifies every signature. For the recorded fixtures and the synthetic book with a flat account, a first --place sends exactly five POST /trade/order requests and a second --place sends none and prints prior for all five. A run whose transport targets open-api.bingx.com returns live_host_refused with no socket opened, and the API key and secret never appear in stdout, stderr or the placement store.

project_specification.integration_points: New modules under packages/router/src/router/: bingx_client.py, bingx_preflight.py, bingx_orders.py and the bingx_mirror.py entry point. Each is committed as an empty stub so its file claim resolves, and each test module beside it in packages/router/tests/ is committed the same way. The client takes an injected transport (a callable from method, URL, headers and body to status and body) and defaults to a urllib transport with a timeout. The host guard runs on the URL before the transport is called, so a test can inject a loopback transport only under the VST host name. There is no setting, environment variable or CLI flag that changes the host. The mirror publishes the book through book.final_target_weights exactly as Stage 0 does, and replaces only its positions field with the VST positions. Orders reach the venue as the Stage 0 BingXOrder parameters (symbol, side, positionSide BOTH, type, quantity, price, timeInForce, clientOrderID). The placement store's idempotency key stays the router's full 64-hex client order identifier, while BingX receives the 40-character projection. The rate limiter is built from a VenueWeightSchedule declared as a module constant in bingx_mirror.py, with weight 1 per request and allowance 10 per second, conservative against BingX's limits; a real 429 is absorbed by retry_rate_limited. Credentials reach the process as environment variables injected by `op run` through run.sh. Wiring them into .env.tpl is done by the operator after the dedicated VST key exists, and is not part of this spec.
project_specification.constraints: - The only host the client can reach is open-api-vst.bingx.com. There is no --live flag, no host setting, and no environment variable that changes it. Feature 321's explicit live flag is out of scope for Stage 1. - No test or task opens a network connection to BingX or anywhere else. Tests use injected transports or the 127.0.0.1 stand-in, with fake credentials. - No task reads 1Password, .env.tpl or any real credential, and none edits .env.tpl, run.sh, claw-forge.yaml or claw-forge.local.yaml. - The API key and secret never appear in a repr, exception message, log line, stdout, stderr or any persisted row. - Nothing is placed without --place, and --place refuses to start without DATABASE_URL, so every placement is recorded and idempotent. - Signing uses the standard library (hmac, hashlib, urllib). The router adds no third-party dependency, and pyproject.toml and uv.lock are not edited. - router.errors, router/__init__.py and the Stage 0 modules (bingx_documents, sizing, bingx_client_order_id, bingx_order, bingx_dry_run) keep their public behaviour, and their tests stay green unchanged. - The fixtures under packages/router/tests/fixtures/bingx_vst/ are inputs and are never edited. - No change to packages/ingest, packages/book's source, packages/risk's source, src/app/module_loader.py, the root pyproject.toml, migrations/** or settings. No new component is registered. - Do not edit docs/user-journeys/: verdicts there are set only by browser runs. - All existing workspace and member tests must stay green.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the client (feature 1). Signing, the host guard, envelope parsing, the 429 mapping, credential loading with redaction, and the nine endpoint methods. Tests use an injected transport that records requests, and pin the signature of a fixed parameter set, timestamp and secret against a value computed independently in the test with hmac.
Phase 2 — preflight and read-back (features 2 and 3), each over an injected client double, with one test per refusal in the stated order.

Phase 3 — the mirror command and the end-to-end test (feature 4). The stand-in is an http.server on 127.0.0.1 that serves the recorded fixtures for the public endpoints, verifies each signed request's signature, keeps a flat account, and counts POST /trade/order requests. The mirror reaches it through the client's injected transport, which rewrites the VST host to 127.0.0.1 inside the test only.
